The Component Reference

content.value: What each block is, how the reader and the edit canvas compare, and exactly what a user can and cannot edit — graded, screenshotted, and code-reviewed. This paper is itself built from the components it documents.

●  paragraph

content.value: · element · insertable.

blocks.text: ●  code

content.value: · element · insertable.
Fully editable: code body is a real textarea, language a real input, and it inserts from the slash menu.

blocks.text: ●  diagram

content.value: · element · insertable.
Fully editable — both Mermaid source and caption are real in-canvas controls and it's slash-insertable, but you edit raw code blind.

items.value: Mermaid source — live monospace textarea, debounced write-back

blocks.text: ●  action

content.value: · element · insertable.
Fully editable in-canvas: label, href, and priority each have a live native control, and the block is slash-insertable.

items.value: Label — text input in the card, debounced commit

— none —

blocks.text: ◐  image

content.value: · element · not insertable.
Barely — a pre-seeded featured slot where you can only swap the picture; nothing else is typed.

items.value: Image — swap via the media picker
Upload — pick from library or upload a new asset
Remove — clears src so the reader skips the block
Alt text — not authorable; derived from the picked asset
Role — read-only, server-painted (Featured image vs Image)
No caption, width, alignment, or link controls
Not insertable — absent from the slash menu, seeded-only

blocks.text: ◐  field-* (native ×7)

content.value: · element · insertable.
All 7 native field types insert and their value edits live in-canvas — but label, schema binding, and select options stay read-only config.

items.value: Field value — real typed control (input/textarea/checkbox/select/date/color)
field-select value — live <select> from the block's inline options
Insert — all 7 types from the slash menu
Persistence — debounced input/change coerces and patches the block
Label — static text, only editable via per-block form or raw JSON
fieldName (schema binding) — attr-only, no canvas UI
Select options set — pickable but not add/remove/rename in-canvas
field-text rows, locked/role attrs — config round-trip only

content.value: Add in-canvas controls for label, fieldName binding, and select-option editing to make the whole field authorable.

blocks.text: ◐  field-image / field-reference

content.value: · element · not insertable.
Narrowly editable — you can set the asset or linked doc in-canvas, but nothing else and you can't even insert one.

items.value: Image asset — ghost frame → media picker writes value
Reference target — typeahead pill picks a doc into value
Both persist via patch-block {value}; undo/echo repaints the picker
label caption — plain read-only text, no input
refType (reference scope) — attr only, no UI
dataset fetch-scope override — attr only, no UI
locked/role doctrine attrs — round-tripped, no UI
field-image has no alt/caption/title — bare asset ref
Not insertable — excluded from slash menu, pick is a no-op

content.value: Add field-image/field-reference to CANVAS_SLASH_TYPES and expose label/refType/dataset as canvas controls.

blocks.text: ◐  composite / arrayOf / codelist / localizedText

content.value: · element · not insertable.
Values of all four composite types are fully editable in the side rail — but you can't insert one, there's no in-canvas editing, and the shape is JSON-only.

items.value: Composite — every subfield gets its native control
arrayOf — text-input rows, add/remove/reorder buttons
codelist — flat picker or stateful tree component
localizedText — one input per configured language
All edits — server-bound, focus-preserving, idempotent
Not insertable — can't add any of the four from the paper
No canvas node-view — renders opaque in the TipTap prose flow
Field shape (subfields, element type, codelist, languages) is JSON-only
Unknown inner field types degrade to read-only atoms
Can't delete the whole block from the paper

content.value: Add canvas node-views + slash-insert entries for all four, plus UI to edit field shape instead of raw JSON.

blocks.text: ●  table

content.value: · widget · insertable.
Genuinely full: cells are real contenteditable inline holes and rows, cols, and header are live buttons.

items.value: Cell text — type directly in each cell, marks round-trip

blocks.text: ◐  card

content.value: · widget · not insertable.
Only title and body edit in-canvas (body silently drops formatting); media/action are raw-string inputs, tone unexposed, card not insertable.

Body rich text — marks flattened to plain text on render

Choosing Your Site Framework

You're about to spawn a site on Barkpark Cloud — a live frontend that reads straight from your content. This guide exists so you can make that choice with open eyes: what each framework is genuinely good at, where it will bite you, and which one fits the site you actually want to ship. There is no single right answer — only the right answer *for your project*.

The short version. For most content sites — blogs, docs, marketing, portfolios — Astro is the best default, and it's the one you can spawn today. If you need a heavily interactive app, you'll want a server-rendered framework like Next.js or TanStack Start. Read on for why.

First, the decision that matters most

Before the framework, understand the axis every framework sits on. It decides your site's speed, cost, and how much can go wrong.

Static (pre-built pages)Server-rendered (SSR)
What it isEvery page is built once into plain HTML/CSS/JSPages are assembled by a live server on each request
SpeedFastest possible — files served from the edgeFast, but every request does work
Cost & scaleEffectively free, scales infinitelyCosts grow with traffic; needs a running process
Best forContent that changes on a human scheduleContent that's personalised or changes per-request
What can breakAlmost nothing at runtimeThe server, under load or on bad input

Barkpark keeps your site and your content on the same wire — the site fetches from your Barkpark project over an internal connection, not the public internet. That means faster builds, private reads, and instant updates when your content changes. Static sites get this at build time; server-rendered sites get it on every request.

Why "close" matters here

• Instant content updates — when you publish in Barkpark, your site knows immediately (no manual redeploy).
• No rate limits, no egress fees — your site reads content over a private link, not a metered public API.
• One login, one domain, one dashboard — the site inherits your workspace, project, and dataset scoping.
• One deploy pipeline — updates roll out with zero downtime, the same way the rest of your Barkpark runs.

The frameworks at a glance

FrameworkLanguageBest atRuntimeShips JS by defaultOn Barkpark Cloud
AstroJS / TSContent sitesStatic or SSRAlmost noneAvailable now
Next.jsJS / TSEverythingStatic or SSRA lotComing
TanStack StartJS / TSInteractive appsSSRA lotComing
SvelteKitJS / TSBothStatic or SSRVery littleComing
NuxtJS / TS (Vue)Content + appStatic or SSRModerateComing
HugoGoContent sitesStatic onlyNoneComing
EleventyJSSimple contentStatic onlyNoneComing
Barkpark Native—Instant sitesRendered for youNoneAvailable now
"Ships JS by default" is a proxy for page weight and speed. Less shipped JavaScript means faster loads and better search rankings — which is why content-first frameworks win on SEO.

The frameworks in depth

Astro — the content-site flagship

Astro is built for exactly what a CMS produces: pages of content. It renders to static HTML by default and only ships JavaScript for the interactive "islands" you explicitly ask for. If you're building a blog, documentation site, marketing site, or portfolio, this is the one to reach for.

Best for: blogs, docs, marketing sites, portfolios, landing pages, changelogs.

Pros

• Blazing fast by design — ships near-zero JavaScript, so pages load instantly and score top marks on Core Web Vitals.
• Built for headless CMS — its content layer is designed to pull from an external source like Barkpark, so the integration is natural, not bolted on.
• Excellent SEO out of the box — fast, static, semantic HTML is what search engines reward.
• Use any UI library — drop in React, Svelte, Vue, or Solid components as islands; you're not locked into one.
• Gentle learning curve — if you know HTML and a little JS, you can be productive in an afternoon.
• Cheapest to host — static output means your site is basically free to serve and scales without limit.
• Grows with you — start static, add server-rendering later for the few pages that need it.
• Huge, active ecosystem of themes and integrations to start from.

Cons

• Not built for app-like UIs — if your site is mostly dashboards, live filtering, or complex client state, Astro's island model fights you.
• Islands take a mental shift — sharing state between separate interactive components is deliberately awkward.
• Smaller component ecosystem than the React/Next world.
• Server-rendering is younger than Next's — battle-tested less at very large scale.
Recommended default, and spawnable today. If you're unsure, start here — you can always graduate to a heavier framework later.

Next.js — the do-everything heavyweight

Next.js is the most popular React framework and can build essentially any kind of site — from a static blog to a full SaaS app. That power comes with weight and complexity.

Best for: apps with logged-in users, dashboards, e-commerce, anything that mixes content with heavy interactivity.

Pros

• Does everything — static pages, server-rendering, and incremental updates all in one framework.
• The largest ecosystem — the most tutorials, templates, integrations, and hireable developers of any framework here.
• Great for interactive apps — if your site has accounts, carts, or dashboards, Next is at home.
• Incremental Static Regeneration — pages can rebuild in the background as content changes, blending static speed with fresh data.
• First-class React — access to the entire React component universe.

Cons

• Heavy — ships a lot of JavaScript, so pages are slower than a static Astro or Hugo site unless carefully tuned.
• Complex — React Server Components and the App Router have a real learning curve, and the "right way" keeps evolving.
• Frequent breaking changes — major versions can mean real migration work.
• Server-rendering costs more to run — dynamic pages need a live process, which grows with traffic.
• Overkill for a brochure site — you'll carry complexity you never use.

TanStack Start — the modern, type-safe challenger

TanStack Start is a newer full-stack React framework built around the excellent TanStack Router. It prioritises end-to-end type safety and a fast, modern developer experience.

Best for: highly interactive, data-heavy applications where type safety and routing power matter.

Pros

• End-to-end type safety — from your routes to your data, mistakes get caught before they ship.
• Best-in-class routing — TanStack Router handles complex, nested, data-driven navigation elegantly.
• Fast, modern tooling — built on Vite, so builds and hot-reload are quick.
• Excellent for interactive apps — streaming server-rendering keeps data-heavy pages snappy.

Cons

• The newest option here — smaller community, fewer templates, fewer answers when you hit a wall.
• Not content-first — overkill for a blog or marketing site.
• Server-rendering runtime — same running-process cost as Next.
• Fewer hireable specialists — a smaller talent pool than React/Next.
• Younger = more risk — APIs are still settling compared to mature frameworks.

SvelteKit — small, fast, and pleasant

SvelteKit compiles your components away at build time, so the browser downloads very little framework code. It handles both static and server-rendered sites and is widely loved for its developer experience.

Best for: teams who want small, fast sites and enjoy a clean, minimal syntax — content or app.

Pros

• Tiny bundles — the framework compiles itself out, so pages are light and fast.
• Loved developer experience — concise syntax, less boilerplate than React.
• Flexible — does static and server-rendering equally well.
• Built-in essentials — routing, data loading, and forms come in the box.

Cons

• Smaller ecosystem than React — fewer ready-made components and integrations.
• Fewer Svelte developers to hire than React developers.
• Server-rendering runtime cost when you choose SSR.
• Less enterprise track record than Next at very large scale.

Nuxt — the Vue powerhouse

Nuxt is to Vue what Next is to React: a mature, full-featured framework for building both content sites and applications. If your team knows Vue, this is the natural home.

Best for: Vue teams building content-rich sites or full applications.

Pros

• Mature and complete — years of production use, batteries included.
• Great content tooling — a dedicated content module makes CMS-driven sites straightforward.
• Does static and server-rendering — flexible per page.
• Approachable — Vue is often considered gentler to learn than React.

Cons

• Smaller talent pool here than React-based options.
• Server-rendering runtime cost identical to Next when you go SSR.
• Ships more JS than an islands or compiled framework like Astro or Svelte.
• Vue-only — you can't borrow the React component universe.

Hugo — the fastest static builder there is

Hugo is a single Go binary that turns content into a static site faster than anything else on this list. No Node.js, no runtime — just files. It's a superb fit for large content sites where build speed matters.

Best for: large blogs, documentation, and content sites where raw build speed and simplicity win.

Pros

• Fastest builds on the market — thousands of pages in seconds.
• No JavaScript runtime needed — a single binary, nothing to keep alive, nothing to patch.
• Cheapest and safest to host — pure static output, no server code to attack.
• Massive theme library — hundreds of ready-made designs.
• Rock-solid and stable — mature, with few breaking changes.

Cons

• Weak on interactivity — no built-in "islands" story; dynamic bits need hand-rolled JavaScript.
• Go templates are clunkier than modern component syntax.
• Not for app-like sites — static only, by design.
• Smaller front-end developer familiarity than the JavaScript frameworks.

Eleventy (11ty) — dead-simple static

Eleventy is a minimalist static site generator. It does very little on purpose, which makes it fast, predictable, and easy to reason about.

Best for: simple content sites where you want maximum control and minimum magic.

Pros

• Extremely simple — little to learn, little to go wrong.
• Zero JavaScript shipped — pages are as light as they get.
• Fast builds and a tiny footprint.
• Template-language freedom — write pages in whichever templating style you like.

Cons

• No interactivity story — you add all dynamic behaviour yourself.
• Very hands-on — the minimalism means more wiring for anything non-trivial.
• Smaller ecosystem than Astro or Next.
• Static only — no server-rendering path.

Barkpark Native — the instant, zero-effort site

Not every site needs a framework. Barkpark can render your content as a live site directly — no build step, no code, no framework to learn. Publish content, get a site. It's the fastest way from "I have content" to "it's online."

Best for: getting content live in seconds, previews, and anyone who doesn't want to touch a framework at all.

Pros

• Instant — live in seconds, with nothing to build or deploy.
• Zero code and zero maintenance — Barkpark handles the rendering and the updates.
• Always in sync — the site *is* your content; there's no separate copy to fall out of date.
• No runtime to pay for or secure — it runs on infrastructure you already have.

Cons

• Barkpark's look, not yours — you theme within what Barkpark offers, rather than designing freely.
• Not for bespoke designs — if you need pixel-level custom layouts, reach for a framework.
• Limited custom interactivity — it's a content site, not an app platform.
Available today. The zero-friction way to get online while you decide whether you need a full framework.

How to choose — by what you're building

If you're building…Start withWhy
A blog or newsletterAstro or Barkpark NativeContent-first, fast, great SEO, minimal fuss
DocumentationAstro or HugoFast static builds, easy navigation, huge page counts
A marketing / landing siteAstroFast, SEO-strong, easy to make beautiful
A portfolioAstro or Barkpark NativeLooks great, ships fast, little to maintain
A site with logins / dashboardsNext.js or TanStack StartServer-rendering handles per-user, interactive pages
An e-commerce storeNext.jsMature ecosystem, handles carts, checkout, and scale
A huge documentation corpusHugoUnbeatable build speed at thousands of pages
"I just want it online now"Barkpark NativeZero build, live in seconds

How your site goes live — and stays live

Every site you spawn deploys the same way, whether it's Astro, Hugo, or Barkpark Native. The process is built around one promise: your live site never goes down, and a broken build never reaches your visitors.

StepWhat happensWhat it means for you
1. TriggerYou click deploy — or you simply publish content and Barkpark rebuilds on its ownNo manual redeploy for content changes
2. Build in isolationYour site is built on separate infrastructure, reading your content over a private linkYour live site keeps serving the whole time
3. Health checkThe new build is tested before anyone sees itA broken build stops here — your current site is untouched
4. Atomic switchThe instant the new build passes, visitors flip to itZero downtime, no half-updated state
5. Instant rollbackThe previous version is kept, ready to restoreIf something's wrong, revert in one click, instantly
Publish-to-live. Change content in Barkpark and your site updates automatically — no redeploy, no waiting, no broken pages in between.

Because your site is built and served right next to your content, deploys are fast and updates are near-instant. There's nothing to wire up: spawn the site, and this pipeline is simply how it works.

What you can spawn today — and what's coming

Barkpark Cloud rolls these out in order of demand. Every framework plugs into the same engine, so the ones marked *coming* are add-ons on a shared foundation, not rewrites.

• Available now: Astro (static) and Barkpark Native (instant).
• Next up: Hugo — proving the same engine serves a second static framework with zero Node runtime.
• Then: Next.js and TanStack Start — server-rendered frameworks, once the secure per-site runtime lands.
• After that: SvelteKit, Nuxt, and Eleventy — filling out the menu.
• Escape hatch: for teams who want a global edge or a fully managed host, Barkpark can also deploy your site to an external platform instead of running it close to your content.
Not sure? Start with Astro. It covers the vast majority of sites beautifully, it's spawnable today, and nothing you build is wasted if you later graduate to a heavier framework.

blocks.text: Interaction doctrine

items.label: D1
items.lead: Gates are optional; auto mode is today's behavior.
items.text: Every gate has a default and (in auto) zero-wait pass-through. The deck adds decision power without taxing the user who trusts the loop.

items.label: D2
items.lead: Research loops are cheap by design.
items.text: “Research more” costs Sonnet-minutes. The deck shows the cost of each option AT the gate, so choosing more research feels safe, not indulgent.

items.label: D3
items.lead: Loops grow one Paper; they never fork.
items.text: Every extra round appends to the same wave Paper. The deck is a lens on the Paper — rewind any wave by scrolling it.

items.label: D4
items.lead: Every gate answer is recorded.
items.text: Choice, author, note, timestamp — appended to the Paper. The wave's story includes the human's decisions, not just the agents'.

items.label: D5
items.lead: The wish never leaves the screen.
items.text: Every gate is judged against it. Persistent, verbatim, untruncated.

blocks.text: Principles the design must carry

items.label: P1
items.lead: Not-found is as loud as found.
items.text: Absence of prior art, a refuted premise, an unreached corner — these change plans. Never render them smaller than positives.

items.label: P2
items.lead: Always show what is in flight.
items.text: The Paper states the plan before each fleet flies; the deck must too. A mid-wave visitor orients in one glance.

items.label: P3
items.lead: Counts with faces.
items.text: “14 agents” is a number; 14 cards with model badges, states, and assignments is a fleet. Aggregate AND enumerate.

items.label: P4
items.lead: Never a bare number.
items.text: Grade travels with commentary; pass travels with the output that produced it; count travels with the list behind it.

items.label: P5
items.lead: Honest states everywhere.
items.text: Agents die, gates go red, streams drop, builders stall. Each is a designed state, not an edge case — loading/empty/error at the Kinsta/Vercel bar.

items.label: P6
items.lead: Drill-down is the trust mechanism.
items.text: Every aggregate opens to its evidence: coverage cell → file+claim, proof row → full output, slice card → bp task, agent card → transcript.

items.label: P7
items.lead: One vocabulary with the ledger.
items.text: Deck states mirror task design language (open/claimed/in_progress/done, criteria met/unmet) — no parallel status taxonomy.

items.value: Deck vs scroll: are slides discrete steps (carousel with the loop map as navigator) or sections of one scrollable live document? The Paper is a scroll; the gates argue for steps.
Where do gate timeouts land — how long does a soft gate wait in attended mode before auto-defaulting, and how is that countdown shown?
Fleet view at 20 agents: cards, rows, or a swarm visualization with detail-on-hover? (80-col TUI parity exists as a constraint worth respecting — the deck should have a terminal projection someday.)
How does the deck coexist with the raw chat transcript — tabs, split, or the deck AS the chat's rich rendering of a wave-scoped session?
Multi-wave epics: does the deck show one wave or the epic's wave history (Paper per wave, charter as the spine)?
Notification surface for gates in unattended mode — push, email, Studio inbox (tickets exists), or all three?

blocks.text: # Aesthetic Unification — Reconciliation Wave of 2026-07-11

**Epic anchor:** `aesthetic-unification-epic` — "Apply the cloud design profile to every Barkpark surface" (priority 1, open).
**Wave status: COMPLETE (2026-07-11)** — all 3 slices built, reviewed grade A-; see the DEBRIEF at the bottom. This Paper is the wave's full story: Digest, Decide, and Review each appended below.
## The wish
Decide honestly whether the anchor's words are fully evidenced:

- **(a)** if "every Barkpark surface" is covered by the shipped 17-artifact lockstep (web reader, Studio, email, TUI, CLI chrome, cloud console, error pages…), stamp the anchor's criteria with file:line + PR evidence and **CLOSE the epic**;
- **(b)** if a surface is genuinely OUTSIDE the lockstep (verify, don't assume: docs-site, web demo app, /activate+login CP pages, barkpark.cloud marketing, PDF/print), cut the **smallest honest wave** to bring it through the SAME manifest — never a parallel token system.

Hard constraints: tokens only via the 3-file lockstep (`design/tokens.json` + `derive.mjs` + `emit.mjs`); `check.mjs` stays green incl. Part F byte-identity and Part H AA; studio-literal-check zero new lit-allows; .ex/.heex waits for Elixir Test; worktrees from origin/main; builders claim first; PR bodies carry `Task: <id>`.
## What the strategist found in five minutes

1. **The lockstep is real and green.** `node design/emit.mjs --check` reports **all 17 artifacts in sync** (16 surfaces + paper-editor mirror): cloud SPA, paper-surface, Studio, /papers reader skin, web demo, web TS tokens, Go board, Go pdrender, Go semrole, Go CLI chrome, Elixir render tokens, Elixir Studio categorical, login (session_html), error page (error_html), status page chrome, /sheets reader, paper-editor mirror.
2. **But the epic ledger says otherwise.** The anchor has **4 acceptance criteria, all `met: false` with empty evidence**, and **23 open children of 55** — including tasks whose own titles say "(SHIPPED)" (`au-w5-paper-components-view`), a full W5.B paper-component-block series (hero, banner, keyvalue, chips, matrix, quote, meter, steps, accordion, sparkline, chart), the W5.D styleguide gallery, W6 brand-mark + visual audit, and one contradiction: `au-w5-pdrender-web-tokens` is open while emit --check lists "Go pdrender: ok".
3. **The wish's candidate gap surfaces are not in the 17-artifact list by name:** email templates (GUI-premium epic shipped 14 email types — through the manifest or past it?), the /activate control-plane page, any marketing/docs site, PDF/print. These need verification, not assumption.
## Strategic direction (tentative — Decide finalizes)

**This is a RECONCILIATION wave, not a build wave.** The system is alive and governing; the ledger is stale. The finished experience: the epic anchor either closed with every criterion stamped `met: true` + file:line + PR evidence, or carrying exactly the honest remainder — and nothing in between.
Three streams, in lean order:

1. **Evidence the 4 anchor criteria.** Each criterion gets concrete file:line + PR/CI proof (manifest single-source, four surface-families adopted, drift gate green in CI, styleguides ratified). If any criterion cannot be evidenced, that IS the wave's work.
2. **Triage the 23 open children into three bins:** (i) *shipped elsewhere* — close with evidence pointing at the PR that shipped it (the PortableDoc showcase, TUI creative slates, and studio-ui-premium epics plausibly absorbed much of W5.B); (ii) *obsolete/superseded* — close as cut with one-line rationale; (iii) *genuinely open* — keep, and decide whether it blocks epic-close or moves to a small named successor task (the epic must not stay open as a component-block wishlist).
3. **Verify the outside-candidates.** Email, /activate CP page, marketing/docs site, PDF/print: for each, either prove it draws from the lockstep (or is out of the anchor's scope with a written rationale) or cut ONE smallest slice through the same manifest. Suspected true gaps: **email** (not in the 17-artifact list) and possibly `--color-graph-canvas` (open child `au-w3-graph-canvas-token`).

**Leaning:** (a)-with-a-small-(b) — stamp and close the anchor this wave, with at most 1-3 surgical build slices (email tokens, graph-canvas token, pdrender-open-task reconciliation) if the verifiers prove real gaps. Tree-tidiness earns nothing; honest evidence earns everything.

## Digest (2026-07-11) — survey folded, verify fleet in flight
**Wave status: VERIFYING** — 8 targeted verifiers launched (plan below). Decide follows their proofs.
### What 15 surveyors established

**1. The lockstep is proven green, twice over.** `node design/emit.mjs --check` = all 17 artifacts in sync; `node design/check.mjs` = Parts A–H PASS (Part F theme-compiler byte-identity, Part H 162/162 WCAG-AA), run live by two independent surveyors AND confirmed in the real CI log (doc-gates run 29128797161 on HEAD 91531b27). Full artifact→consumer map is now on record (survey `lockstep-inventory`).

**2. The wish's four candidate gap surfaces mostly dissolved on contact:**
- **Email — NOT a gap.** The "14 GUI-premium email types" are the 14 PortableDoc fleet block types rendered `:email` for the mailed-paper view, and they draw through `Palettes.email_skin → TokensGen` = artifact #11/17 (`api/lib/barkpark/portable_doc/render/tokens_gen.ex`, generated from tokens.json `paperEmail`). One documented literal exception (terminal traffic-dots, `panels_email.ex:104-106`, charter D4). Role tones ride `design/status-manifest.json` (a governed sibling manifest — evidence wording must say "tokens.json + status-manifest.json", not "tokens.json alone"). Transactional emails (reset/invite/digest) are plain text — no aesthetic surface at all.
- **/activate + CP login — NOT a gap.** All CP routes (`/`, `/dashboard`, `/new`, `/activate`) serve one SPA (`router.ex:317-348` → `index.html:14` → `app.css`), and `app.css` IS the "cloud SPA" lockstep artifact (emit.mjs:1720). Login/signup are JS modes of the same screen.
- **Marketing/docs site — scope-cut.** barkpark.cloud is served by web/ (in lockstep as "web demo" + "web TS tokens"). `js/docs/` (Fumadocs) is genuinely outside the lockstep but is a known-dormant, unwired, undeployed app — pre-existing decision record at `docs/decisions/deferred.md:8`. Tokenizing an unserved site earns nothing.
- **PDF/print — scope-cut.** No PDF pipeline exists anywhere (repo-wide grep clean). Print = tokenized `@media print` blocks in both reader layouts (`sheets.html.heex:261-277`, `bulldocs.html.heex:838-878`) with exactly one frozen paper-white literal each (exemptions.json:13, PR #2273).

**3. Real gaps surfaced where nobody guessed:**
- **Literal-color residue (contests criterion 1).** Using check.mjs Part E's own counting rule: ~880 un-ledgered literal hits across ~104 files beyond the 4 frozen exemption files. Top offenders: `api/assets/paper-editor/src/styles.css` 181 (dead `var(--paper-x, #hex)` fallbacks — the exact anti-pattern the root.html.heex sweep purged) + its web mirror 107; `bp-graph.js` byte-identical pair 91×2 (hand-authored Canvas2D palette, zero token consumption); `paper-surface.css` 51 (the source-of-truth file itself is never counted anywhere); `tickets/inbox_live.ex` 48; `tasks/web/board_live.ex` 32 (raw unwrapped hex, no var() at all); `sheets.html.heex` 31 (a THIRD independent hand-set `--paper-*` block). Raw tally includes test-fixture/generated noise — needs a judgment pass before it decides C1.
- **web portable-doc.tsx (the real half of `au-w5-pdrender-web-tokens`).** The live /papers+post web reader hand-codes callout tones as a literal Tailwind palette map (`portable-doc.tsx:256-266`) with no relationship to tokens.json — a parallel color system on a flagship surface. The Go pdrender half of the same task is DONE, shipped under theme-system PRs #1395/#1691/#1984; criterion wording "via semrole" is architecturally false by design (pdrender may never import semrole; it gets a byte-identical emitted copy).
- **Graph-canvas token** (`au-w3-graph-canvas-token`) — confirmed real, small, self-documented at `graph-landing.tsx:56`. The Studio Canvas2D graph (bp-graph.js) is a separate, bigger problem and NOT in that task's scope.
- **Brand mark (`au-w6-brand-mark`) — genuine and unabsorbed.** No logo asset exists anywhere; three surfaces brand three ways; favicons diverge (web = real ICO, api = 152-byte PNG mislabeled .ico, cloud = NONE). Needs a human-drawn mark + sign-off — wrong shape for a surgical slice; spin-off candidate (with a possible tiny "one favicon everywhere" mechanical sub-slice).

**4. Anchor criteria honest state:** C1 contested by the residue finding (stampable only with an exemptions-extension or fix slices — verifier decides which). C2 met with the documented email nuance (brand/rule hex deliberately pinned to email-golden, tokens_gen.ex:11-14 says "w3 reconciles the two" — did w3 run? unverified). C3 green-on-every-run but NOT GitHub-enforced (branch protection 404; rulesets API not yet queried — evidence must say "blocking CI step, team-enforced" unless rulesets says otherwise). The 11 `au-w5-comp-*` + `au-w5-paper-components-view` were fabricated-done (identical boilerplate, null claim) and reopened 2026-07-08; the blocks (hero…sparkline) do not exist in compose.ex's ~50-type registry; issue #1475 open, no PR anywhere. # DECIDE — 2026-07-11 (Fable)

Two rounds of ground truth in; charter written and COMMITTED+PUSHED (`.claude/workflows/bp-cloud-epic-charter.md`, commit 94313d04 — composition-doctrine's occupancy preserved verbatim at `bp-composition-doctrine-charter.md`).
## What the verify round proved (and refuted)

**residue-c1-verdict — C1 is NOT stampable today; one ledger slice away.** Decisive: "TOTAL frozen: 329 | UN-LEDGERED … sum=646" against exemptions.json, and "studio-literal-check: PASS — 219 files scanned" while never scanning `api/lib/barkpark/plugins` (WEB var pins the walk to `barkpark_web`) — two LIVE LiveViews (inbox_live.ex 48, board_live.ex 32) invisible to every gate. blocks.text: # Authoring Excellence — Wave 5: Finish & Land the Held Wall

*Living wave paper. Opened at Strategize (2026-07-13). Every later phase appends here — Digest folds the survey, Decide records the wave plan, Review closes the story. Workers never write this paper; they write their own bp task.*

Epic: `authoring-excellence` · Charter: `.claude/workflows/bp-authoring-excellence-charter.md` (authoritative over the design paper). Prior waves: wave-2026-07-10 (wall built), -07-12 (D10 window closed, search payoff), -07-12b (feedback rings), -07-13 (last bypass extracted). This wave (07-13b): **make the extraction's full-suite gate actually green.**
## The situation

Wave 4 built the flagship: one shared `Barkpark.Content.AuthoringWall.enforce/5` — a single fail-closed door for every published paper AND task, whether born through `lifecycle.publish_document` or `BlockOps.upsert_paper`. PR #2881 (branch `loop-epic/ae-w4-seal-last-bypass-integrated`) carries the extraction + a 114-callsite fixture sweep + the editor legacy-tag fix. The wave-4 review stamped it "SEALED, grade A-".

But that green was **directory-scoped** (content+papers 829/0, web-controllers+studio 2154/1) — NOT the full suite. `CC=/usr/bin/clang mix test` is **RED with 6 failures**, all one class: an untagged PAPER publish returns 422 `label_spine`. These ~5 flows publish papers via HTTP mutate / LiveView / a projection seam — NOT the swept `upsert_paper(attrs)` helper — so the fixture sweep never touched them. The wall works exactly as designed; the fixtures never learned to carry tags on these paths.
## The wish (verbatim intent)

FINISH and LAND the held wall. Resume from `loop-epic/ae-w4-seal-last-bypass-integrated` (rebase on current origin/main — 2 commits ahead: #2883 mutate double-nesting warn, #2882 portabledoc reader). Make the 6 flows pass by registering weighted tags in each flow's setup (`LabelFixtures.register_tags!`) + adding them to the paper mutate/LiveView payload — the SAME tag-spine the fixture-sweep applied, extended to the API/LiveView paper-creation paths. Fail-before / pass-after per flow. Then `CC=/usr/bin/clang mix test` must be FULLY green (the co-dependency check). Do NOT touch the wall's type scope (`@walled_types ~w(paper task)`; sheets/posts unwalled). Do NOT re-extract the wall. Do NOT reopen `ae-w4-ratchet-telemetry` (#2817 correctly landed). Also fold in D36 `ae-ingest-advisory-deadletter` if tractable as a SEPARATE opus slice.
## The 6 failing flows (5 files)

- `api/test/barkpark/sheets_m0_proof_test.exs` — publishes via `POST /v1/data/mutate`; the sheet-backed paper projection falls through to `upsert_paper`.
- `api/test/barkpark/sheets_m1_proof_test.exs` — **TWO failures**: the M1 write-through story AND the "two colleagues edit the budget live" LiveView collab test.
- `api/test/barkpark_web/controllers/bulldocs_email_controller_test.exs` — publishes a paper via the email-controller path.
- `api/test/barkpark_web/integration/preview_routes_test.exs` — creates/publishes a paper to exercise preview routes.
## Strategic direction

This is a **FINISH wave**, not a design wave. The wall is correct and must not move. The disciplined outcome: the full suite goes green because EACH failing flow carries a registered, weighted tag on its paper-publish payload — the exact tag-spine the sweep applied, now reaching the HTTP-mutate / LiveView / projection birth paths the sweep couldn't see. Fail-before/pass-after evidence per flow; then the whole `CC=/usr/bin/clang mix test` green as the co-dependency proof.

**THE ONE QUESTION THAT DECIDES THE FIX SHAPE** (survey must resolve it): are these TEST-ONLY fixture gaps, or do they expose an UNAUDITED PRODUCTION paper-birth path? If a real sheet publish, a real email-controller publish, or a real preview generation projects an untagged paper in prod, the honest fix is **product code** (the projection seam threads synthesized tags OR carries an explicit `bypass_wall: true` + rationale, exactly as D26 audited the lib callers) — and the test merely proves it. If they are pure fixtures birthing test papers, the wish's "register tags in setup + payload" is right and the change is test-only.

I LEAN toward **honest per-flow classification**: genuinely-authored publishes (email, collab budget doc) carry tags; machine PROJECTIONS (sheet view, preview render) that were never meant to be search-findable carry a product-code bypass with a grep-able rationale — the same doctrine D26 used for plan_papers and seeds. Decide finalizes after two explore rounds.

**Quality bar (Kinsta/Vercel):** a rejected publish must cost an agent ONE retry with a machine-readable error — never a silent 422 on a path a real user hits. So if any of these 6 is a live prod path, shipping test-only tags would leave prod broken. The verify fleet must check prod reality, not just the test tree.
## Model constraint & shape

Fable EXHAUSTED. Every `builder_model = opus`; decompose too-hard slices into smaller opus slices; NEVER Haiku. Verify fleet: opus for correctness digs, sonnet only for breadth mapping. Primary slice resumes the held branch, rebases on origin/main, fixes ONLY the ~5 non-fixture paper-publish flows, proves full green. Optional second opus slice: D36 `ae-ingest-advisory-deadletter` — but it COLLIDES with the primary on `bulldocs_ingest_controller.ex`, so sequence it, don't parallelize. Main checkout stays on main; all builds in isolated worktrees; gate Elixir in the integration worktree (build-borrow-broken). `.ex/.exs/.heex` WAIT for the Elixir Test gate before merge.
## IN FLIGHT: surveying

14 broad Sonnet surveyors are mapping each failing flow's exact paper-publish seam, whether it is test-only or a real prod path, the `LabelFixtures` API surface for extending to payloads, the wave-4 `bypass_wall` audit gaps, the full-suite gate co-dependency, the rebase delta, and D36 tractability. Digest distills the reports into the verify plan; Decide rules the per-flow fix shape (tags vs product bypass) before builders fly.
## DIGEST — survey folded, verify fleet in flight (2026-07-13)
*14 broad surveyors reported. Trust file:line evidence over prose. This section replaces "IN FLIGHT: surveying" — the wave is now **verifying**.*
### What the survey ESTABLISHED (high-confidence, multiply-confirmed)

1. **The wall is built and correct on the held branch.** `@walled_types ~w(paper task)`, unchanged on both main and `loop-epic/ae-w4-seal-last-bypass-integrated`. Sheets/posts are structurally unwalled. Do NOT touch scope — confirmed by 6 surveyors via `git show`.
2. **The ingest controller ALREADY carries the D26 tags/description passthrough on the branch.** `bulldocs_ingest_controller.ex` threads `params["tags"]/params["description"]` into `Content.upsert_paper(attrs)` on BOTH the blocks-head and the legacy-HTML-head, with explicit "charter D26" comments and `{:error,{:label_spine,_}}/{:unknown_tag,_}/{:duplicate_of,_}` → `render_error` routing. Six surveyors confirmed this on the branch. **One dissent** (labelfixtures-api) claims the whitelist OMITS tags/description — but that read was against **main** (pre-wave-4), not the branch. Load-bearing contradiction → verified this round.
3. **Sheet publish is not a prod 422 risk.** The sheet→paper write-through (`sheets.ex refresh_doc_sheet_snapshots`) refreshes an already-published paper's embed cache via a raw `Document.changeset |> Repo.update()` — it never calls `upsert_paper`/`AuthoringWall`. Papers that embed sheets are born through the SAME audited ingest endpoint as any paper. No sheets-specific paper-birth path exists.
4. **The failing flows birth their paper via HTTP `POST /v1/plugins/bulldocs/papers`** (bulldocs ingest) — NOT via the Elixir-level `upsert_paper(` bind the wave-4 grep-sweep wrapped. That is exactly why the sweep (114 callsites / 40 files, all `upsert_paper(` literals) missed them. The fix shape is: register weighted tags in setup + add `tags`/`description` to the ingest POST body.
5. **`bulldocs_email_controller` is READ-ONLY** (`GET /papers/:slug/email` → `get_public_paper` + render). It cannot 422 a real user. Its test's 422 comes purely from its own `ingest!` fixture setup. There is NO inbound email→paper ingest anywhere (gen_smtp is outbound-only). Pure test-fixture gap.
6. **Prod reality:** the wave-4 `upsert_paper` mount is NOT deployed on guerrilla (only the wave-1 lifecycle wall is). So no live incident today. BUT real ingest-create traffic (`POST /v1/plugins/bulldocs/papers`, dozens/day, all 200) is currently unwalled — once the mount merges fail-closed, if D26 passthrough is not solid, that real traffic starts 422ing. That is the one CONCRETE prod-risk surface (not sheets, not email).
### Where the survey CONTRADICTS the wish / direction (Decide must reconcile)

- **preview_routes_test.exs does not fit the failure class.** FIVE surveyors independently found it creates ONLY type `"post"` (unwalled) — never a paper/task. One surveyor RAN it standalone on main: **11 tests, 0 failures**. It structurally cannot self-produce a label_spine 422. Either the wish's file list is stale for this name, or its full-suite red (if any) is cross-test pollution (`async: false` + global `Application.put_env(:barkpark, :preview, …)`) or the #2886 `RequireWithinQuota` plug — NOT a missing tag. Adding tags here would be a no-op that leaves the real red.
- **sheets_m1_proof_test.exs holds ONE test, not two, and it is HTTP not LiveView.** "two colleagues edit the budget live" IS the file's sole test (`use ConnCase`, driven over `build_conn`), and it births its paper via the same ingest POST — there is no separate "M1 story" test and no LiveView collab test anywhere. - **The named 5/6 UNDERCOUNTS.** `sheets_m3_proof_test.exs` and `sheets_m3_m5_proof_test.exs` use the identical untagged ingest pattern, were NOT in the 40-file sweep, and have zero branch-unique commits — almost certainly ALSO red. Building fixes for only the named 5 could leave 2 files red and the full-suite gate still failing.
- **Rebase delta is 5–6 commits, not 2.** True fork point is `821fcada`; origin/main is 5 ahead. #2882 (portabledoc render) and #2883 (mutate double-nesting warn) touch disjoint regions; #2886 (Perfect Plan W1) touches `lifecycle.ex`+`mutations.ex` in disjoint hunks AND adds a `RequireWithinQuota` plug on `:scoped_mutate` — a NEW rebase risk (could 402/403 test flows). Line-range comparison predicts clean rebase but it was NOT executed.
### The decision-shaping fork (unchanged, sharpened)

Test-only fixture gap vs. unaudited production paper-birth path. Survey weight says **test-only for the genuinely-authored ingest flows** (sheets_m0/m1, bulldocs_email) — the product-code half (D26 passthrough) already shipped on the branch; only the test payloads lag. The honest exceptions the direction named (machine projections carry a grep-able `bypass_wall` rationale) do NOT arise here because none of the failing flows is a projection — they are real ingest publishes. **The fork now hinges on TWO runtime facts:** (a) does adding tags to ONE flow's payload actually make it green on the branch (proves passthrough works → test-only), and (b) what is the ACTUAL full-suite red list on the rebased branch (settles preview_routes scope + m3/m3_m5 undercount). Both are RUN this round.
### Coverage map — checked & FOUND vs checked & NOT-FOUND (absences are decisions-in-waiting)

**FOUND (settled by evidence):**
- Ingest controller D26 passthrough present on branch — `git show` (6 surveyors).
- `@walled_types ~w(paper task)` unchanged — branch + main.
- sheet write-through bypasses wall (raw Repo.update) — `sheets.ex:151-159`.
- email controller read-only — `bulldocs_email_controller.ex:28-49`.
- sheets_m0/m1, bulldocs_email all POST to `/v1/plugins/bulldocs/papers` untagged — test files.
- `LabelFixtures.paper_attrs/2` exists on branch ONLY (not main); `register_tags!`/`weighted_labels`/`with_registered_labels` are the test-side spine.
- preview_routes creates only `post`; passes 11/0 standalone on main.
- Prod: wave-4 mount NOT on guerrilla; ingest-create traffic live+unwalled; 2 live sheet-embedding papers (portabledoc-showcase, fleet-audit) untagged but pre-existing → grandfathered by Exemptions ledger.
- D36 tractable, small, collides on `bulldocs_ingest_controller.ex` case-blocks → sequence-after; D27 prerequisite done.
- mix test does NOT hit codelist-OOM (test.exs disables seeders); local worktrees not shallow (git tags fine); CC=/usr/bin/clang required whole-chain; MIX_TEST_PARTITION needed to avoid DB collision.

**NOT-FOUND (open — corners no surveyor closed):**
- **No surveyor RAN the full suite on the rebased branch.** Every "these 6 fail" claim is static-derived; box had a concurrent `mix test` so surveyors backed off. The real red list is unproven.
- **preview_routes' actual full-suite failure** (if any) — root cause never observed (standalone green only).
- **Whether the rebase is truly clean** — predicted by line-ranges, never executed.
- **Whether #2886 `RequireWithinQuota` 402/403s any failing flow** post-rebase — flagged, unverified.
- **Complete blast radius** — only the named files + m3/m3_m5 were spot-checked; no exhaustive census of ALL untagged walled-publish test flows.
- **The labelfixtures-api ↔ six-surveyor contradiction** on the branch controller — not reconciled by a direct branch read in that report.
- **bp search** — no surveyor could run it (`bp search` is not a verb; it's `search.query`); the Barkpark FTS prior-art angle went uncovered (grep substituted).
### VERIFY FLEET — in flight now (drives tasks filed at Decide)

1. **keystone-red-and-probe** (opus, worktree) — Rebase the held branch on origin/main (report clean/conflicts), cold-compile, run the FULL `mix test`, capture the EXACT failing `file::test` list with each error line. Confirm/refute: are m3 + m3_m5 red? is preview_routes red and with what assertion (label_spine or not)? any 402/403? Then probe sheets_m0 + bulldocs_email: fail-before → apply ONLY a test-payload tag fix → pass-after. **Proves** the test-only-vs-product-code fork and the passthrough contradiction by RUNNING, not reading.
2. **untagged-publish-census** (sonnet) — Grep the entire `api/test` tree for EVERY walled-type (paper/task) birth via ingest POST / mutate-publish / LiveView save that lacks weighted tags; diff against the 40-file sweep list. Emits the COMPLETE candidate red set so Decide scopes the primary task to all sweep-missed flows, not just the named 5.
3. **preview-and-quota-diagnosis** (opus) — Trace the router plug pipeline for the preview + scoped-mutate routes; determine whether preview_routes' alleged red is (a) stale wish, (b) global-state cross-test pollution, or (c) the #2886 quota plug — and whether that plug threatens the paper-birth flows. Tells Decide if preview_routes is in scope at all.
4. **branch-passthrough-and-charter-confirm** (opus) — Settle the labelfixtures-api dissent by reading the BRANCH controller directly (`git show` both heads); confirm the honest per-flow classification against charter D26/D23-b/D6 — no flow needs `bypass_wall`, none needs a wall-scope change, every named flow is a test-payload fix.
*Decide finalizes the per-flow fix shape and files/perfects the slice tasks after this fleet lands.*
## Decide (2026-07-13) — decisions ratified, wave plan filed
*Appended by the Decide phase. 4-verifier deep round with full-suite RUN proofs settled the fork. Charter D39–D42 are authoritative; this mirrors them.*
### Verification results — what was proven / refuted

- **keystone-red-and-probe (SETTLED, run proof).** Ran the full suite on the REBASED branch: `27 doctests, 10355 tests, 5 failures` — every failure a `label_spine` 422 on untagged PAPER ingest. Rebase onto `origin/main` is CLEAN (`Successfully rebased and updated`, 4 commits, zero conflicts — re-run at Decide, same result). The D26 tags/description passthrough IS present on the branch (`bulldocs_ingest_controller.ex:99-100` + `:167-168`) so the fix is TEST-ONLY. Probe: `register_tags! + payload tags/description` on 2 of the 5 files → `4 tests, 0 failures`. `#2886 RequireWithinQuota` emits ZERO 402/403 in the whole run.
- **untagged-publish-census (run-proven).** The true red set is 5 files: `sheets_m0/m1/m3/m3_m5_proof` + `bulldocs_email_controller`. `sheets_m3` + `sheets_m3_m5` were NOT named by the wish but ARE red (same untagged `POST /v1/plugins/bulldocs/papers`); a fix limited to the wish's names leaves 2 reds. `sheets_m1_proof_test.exs` has exactly ONE test (HTTP `ConnCase`, not LiveView).
- **preview-and-quota-diagnosis + charter-decision-consistency.** `preview_routes_test.exs` is GREEN and out of scope — it births only unwalled type `post`, is byte-identical to a green `main`, and structurally cannot emit `label_spine`. Coverage NOT-FOUND: no unaudited production paper-birth path (every red flow rides the already-D26-audited ingest endpoint); no boot/background path births a walled doc; `RequireWithinQuota` absent on the branch (rebase inherits it, inert).
- **branch-passthrough-and-charter-confirm.** DISSENT refuted with proof: the "passthrough missing" claim read `main`, not the branch — `git diff` shows the 8-line insert on both heads is branch-only. `@walled_types ~w(paper task)` unchanged (`authoring_wall.ex:68`).
### Decisions (mirror the charter D39–D42)

- **D39 — Fork is TEST-ONLY.** Full-suite run + probe prove it; passthrough already present ⇒ fix is fixture payloads on 5 files, zero product code, no `bypass_wall`, no wall re-scope.
- **D40 — True red set is 5 files.** `preview_routes` green/out; `sheets_m1` is one HTTP test; `sheets_m3` + `sheets_m3_m5` unnamed-but-red and in scope; quota inert.
- **D41 — Rebase clean; primary owns it.** 4 commits, zero conflicts (proven twice); primary rebases + force-pushes so slice 2 branches off the rebased tip.
- **D42 — D36 ships as a file-disjoint second opus slice.** Primary is test-only (no lib source), so no controller collision; D36's targeted gate proves independently; it stacks on the primary's tip for an honest full-suite run.
### Wave plan (2 opus slices — Fable exhausted, all builders opus)

| # | Task id | Surface | Model | Size | Gate |
|---|---------|---------|-------|------|------|
| 1 | `ae-w5-finish-publish-wall` | Elixir tests (5 files) | opus | medium | `cd api && export CC=/usr/bin/clang CXX=/usr/bin/clang++ && MIX_ENV=test mix test test/barkpark/sheets_m0_proof_test.exs test/barkpark/sheets_m1_proof_test.exs test/barkpark/sheets_m3_proof_test.exs test/barkpark/sheets_m3_m5_proof_test.exs test/barkpark_web/controllers/bulldocs_email_controller_test.exs` (targeted) → then full `CC=/usr/bin/clang MIX_ENV=test mix test` (co-dependency seal, 0 failures) |
| 2 | `ae-ingest-advisory-deadletter` | Elixir ingest controller + docs | opus | small | `cd api && CC=/usr/bin/clang MIX_ENV=test mix test test/barkpark_web/controllers/bulldocs_ingest_controller_test.exs` |

**Sequencing:** Slice 1 lands PR #2881 (the wave-4 stack — `ae-upsert-paper-wall` + `ae-fixture-sweep` + `ae-editor-legacy-tag-writeloss` all ride the branch and close on merge). Slice 2 branches off slice 1's rebased/force-pushed tip; file sets are disjoint so its targeted gate proves independently. Main checkout stays on main; all builds in isolated worktrees; gate Elixir IN the worktree; `.ex/.exs/.heex` wait for the full Elixir Test gate before merge; the LEAD closes each merge-gated criterion.
**Backlog filed this wave:** `ae-preview-routes-pollution-guard` (priority 3 — speculative test-isolation hardening; `preview_routes` is green today, never observed red).
## REVIEW — the wave's debrief (2026-07-13, reviewer wf_e5126c6a)

*Closes the story. One Fable reviewer, last hands before merge: reviewed both green slices in an isolated worktree with a borrowed-deps / copied `_build/test` Elixir gate, re-ran every gate, fixed what was wrong, audited the ledger.*
### What shipped

**Slice 1 — `ae-w5-finish-publish-wall` (primary).** Final branch `loop-epic/ae-w4-seal-last-bypass-integrated` (PR #2881), reviewed at tip `c94a5ac6` + a reviewer format-only commit (`ae-w5-review` ref `9990c82d`). The fix is exactly what D39 predicted: TEST-ONLY, 5 files, `+79` lines, zero `api/lib`. Each of the 5 untagged HTTP-ingest paper-birth flows (`sheets_m0/m1/m3/m3_m5_proof` + `bulldocs_email_controller`) gained `@wall_tags` (3 distinct-strength weighted tags, unique max, ≥20-char rationales) + `@wall_description` + `LabelFixtures.register_tags!(@dataset, names)` in setup, with tags/description merged into the `POST /v1/plugins/bulldocs/papers` body. Reviewer re-ran the targeted gate: **11 tests, 0 failures**. Non-vacuousness re-proven: reverting the tag payload on `sheets_m0` reds the flow with a `422 label_spine` (the wall genuinely enforces; the fix genuinely satisfies it). `@walled_types ~w(paper task)` unchanged (`authoring_wall.ex:68`); `preview_routes` untouched.

**Slice 2 — `ae-ingest-advisory-deadletter` (D36/D42).** Builder branch `loop-epic/ingest-advisory-dead-letter-wire-warning-1` @ `ac6e7a0c`; reviewed as `ae-ingest-advisory-r` — a **clean cherry-pick of `ac6e7a0c` onto the rebased primary tip** (the honest integration; the builder branch still sat on the pre-rebase wave-4 stack, the documented base-drift). `bulldocs_ingest_controller.ex` opens the request-scoped advisory channel with `Warnings.reset()` before `Content.upsert_paper` on BOTH ingest heads and folds `Warnings.drain()` into the 200 body via a `with_warnings/1` helper (additive `warnings: [{code,severity,message}]`, **omitted when empty → byte-identical pre-wall body**) — a faithful mirror of `mutate_controller.ex:17-29`. Reviewer re-ran the gate: **31 tests, 0 failures**. Non-vacuous: reverting only the controller lib reds the trip test (`warnings=nil`). `docs/api-v1.md` §6 documents the shape change; `check-doc-budgets.sh` green (13994 ≤ 14000B). The cherry-pick onto the primary is conflict-free (incl. `api-v1.md`).
### The full-suite co-dependency seal — the honest picture
The wish's hard gate is `CC=/usr/bin/clang mix test` FULLY green. Reviewer ran it TWICE on the primary tip (seed 1, isolated worktree build):

- **Run 1:** `27 doctests, 10355 tests, 1 failure` — an order-dependent failure that **passed in isolation** (`mix test --failed` → 0 failures).
- **Run 2:** `27 doctests, 10355 tests, 1 failure` — the sole failure was `BarkparkWeb.PulsePublicSurfaceTest` "per-IP burst cap yields 429" (`assert count(200s) == 3` got `4` — a rate-limiter boundary race); a concurrent `Postgrex` owner-exited sandbox disconnect logged alongside it.

**The two runs failed on DIFFERENT, unrelated tests — never `label_spine`, never a paper/wall path.** The suite is not deterministically green even at a fixed seed: it carries pre-existing async-timing / sandbox-ownership flakes (rate-limit burst caps, DB connection ownership, the D40-named `preview_routes` `Application.put_env` pollution, chat-spawn timing) in subsystems entirely disjoint from this wave. The builder's "seed 1 = 0 failures" was one lucky run, not a reproducible guarantee — **corrected here**: the wall fix is solid (no wall failure in any run; every target flow green in isolation and in the targeted gate), and the residual full-suite reds are environmental. **CI on PR #2881 may need a re-run to clear a flake — that is a re-run, not a wall regression.**
### Reviewer fixes applied

1. **Format drift (this wave's own).** The 5 `@wall_tags` map literals exceeded the line limit; the base files were format-clean, so the drift was introduced by the wave-5 commit. `mix format` re-flowed all 5 (multi-line maps) — committed as `9990c82d` on the reviewed primary ref. Targeted gate still 11/0. (Format is an advisory gate; fixed for cleanliness.)
2. **Advisory integration.** Produced the correct stacked state (`ac6e7a0c` cherry-picked onto the rebased primary) that the builder's branch had not — proven clean, gate 31/0.
### Ledger audit

- **`ae-w5-finish-publish-wall` — one real defect, FIXED.** The acceptance-criteria evidence was **shifted by one slot** throughout, and the terminal MERGE-GATED criterion (#4, "PR #2881 merged") was **falsely `met=true`** carrying criterion-3's diff-stat evidence — a board would have read the flagship PR as already merged. Reviewer realigned all evidence to its rightful criterion (0–3 `met=true` with correct proof + reviewer re-verification notes) and reset #4 to `met=false` (the LEAD closes it on merge). `lifecycle_status` correctly `in_progress`.
- **`ae-ingest-advisory-deadletter` — honest.** Criteria 0–2 `met=true` with accurate evidence; the merge-gated #3 `met=false`; `in_progress`. No fix needed.
- No task outside this wave was touched. Backlog `ae-preview-routes-pollution-guard` confirmed filed (the flakes above are exactly its remit).
### Grade — A−

The wave does precisely what the wish asked, at the right altitude: a minimal, correct, test-only finish that satisfies the fail-closed wall on all five HTTP-ingest flows, plus a clean, additive advisory-dead-letter slice that recovers a real dropped signal — both non-vacuously proven, file-disjoint, cross-coherent. The flagship (`AuthoringWall.enforce` guarding every paper birth, lifecycle AND ingest) is genuinely ready to land. Docked from A for two honesty gaps the reviewer had to close: the ledger's shifted evidence with a **falsely-met merge-gated criterion** (a real lie, now fixed), and the **overclaimed "full suite green"** (the suite is green only modulo pre-existing environmental flakes — true and important for the lead to know before trusting a single CI run). Neither is a defect in the wall or the fix; both are discipline slips around an otherwise excellent finish.
### Correction to earlier sections

This paper's title and its "6 failing flows" / `preview_routes` / "LiveView collab test" framing (Situation, §"The 6 failing flows") were the wave's opening hypothesis; **Decide/D40 superseded them** — the true red set is 5 files, `preview_routes` is green and out of scope (unwalled `post`), and `sheets_m1` holds one HTTP test, not a LiveView collab test. The Decide section already carries this reconciliation; noted here so a reader trusts D40 over the opening.
### What the next wave takes

Backlog only — the wall is complete. `ae-paper-decision-sync` (WIDENED: full D18–D42 table regen, all design-paper anchors stale), `ae-curator-feed` (persisted findings, deferred until a consumer exists), `ae-dedup-trgm-index` (rewrite DedupWall `similarity()>0.1` to the `%` operator before any type holds thousands of published docs), `ae-w4-findability-posttest` (D9 Oban self-query — filed, unbuilt), `ae-search-eval-baseline-repair`, `ae-boot-gate-ci`, `ae-js-sdk-strength-filter`, and `ae-preview-routes-pollution-guard` (harden the `async:false` `Application.put_env(:barkpark,:preview,…)` cross-test pollution the full-suite flakes exposed). None blocks the north star.

blocks.text: # bp mcp serve — Reconcile-and-Close Wave of 2026-07-11

**Epic anchor:** `bp-mcp-serve-epic` — "bp mcp serve — MCP server for Barkpark Tasks (Cursor path B)". 8/8 children done, every child criterion met, epic still `open`. *(Correction, Review 2026-07-11: the epic is now `done`+published — see the Debrief below.)*
## The Wish (verbatim)

Verify the anchor's own criteria at HEAD, stamp with the PR trail (#1790/#1791/#1993 + the #2588 transport as corroborating evidence, cited cross-epic by id+sha per the dedup law), and CLOSE the epic if its words are fully evidenced — the ledger sweep pattern. If the anchor names genuinely unbuilt scope, name the honest remainder or re-home it. Zero build slices expected; every stamp = file:line + PR + run evidence. Hard laws: never close over an unverified criterion; publish-collapse any drafts.* touch; human gates stay open with recipes; builders claim first if any slice exists.
## Strategy (wave direction)

This is a **zero-build reconciliation wave**. The finished experience: the epic closed with a stamp trail where every clause of the anchor's description is matched to evidence at HEAD — file:line in `internal/cli/mcp_*.go`, the owning PR, and a fresh run proof (stdio smoke + go test at HEAD, not a memory of green). The #2588 remote transport and #2580 task_stamp/task_pulse tools are **corroborating cross-epic evidence** (cited by id+sha, owned elsewhere) proving the stdio core this epic built became the shared seam for two later epics — the strongest possible "done" signal.

Leaning toward CLOSE. Anchor scope check: core five tools (task_ready, task_next, task_show, task_close, task_create) → w1-core; manifest-machinery reuse → w1-seam; stretch bridge → w1-bridge; Cursor docs → w1-docs; plus w2 (catalog/resources/validation). Two suspected wrinkles the fleets must settle:

1. **Naming drift** — the anchor says `task_show`; the CLI verb is `task get`. Is the MCP tool actually named `task_show` at HEAD, or did it drift? A rename is fine, but the stamp must say so honestly.
2. **Doc staleness** — did #2588 (--http) or #2580 (new tools) leave CURSOR.md / HANDBOOK / `docs/ops/mcp-serve-validation.md` describing a smaller server than HEAD ships? Staleness is at most a residue task, not a blocker, unless a documented recipe is now WRONG.
OAuth for Claude.ai remote is **explicitly not this epic's scope** — it is viable-everywhere w3. The close-out will disclaim it by name so nobody reopens this epic for it.
## Survey plan (in flight NOW — 13 Sonnet surveyors)

1. **anchor-criteria** — What exactly are the anchor's own words/criteria (raw doc at HEAD)? Does the epic doc carry acceptance_criteria of its own, or only the description + children? → defines the exact checklist we must evidence before closing.
2. **core-tools-at-head** — Do the five curated task tools exist at HEAD in `internal/cli/mcp_tasks.go`/`mcp_serve.go`? Exact registered tool names (task_show vs task_get drift), file:line map. → the stamp's core evidence; naming drift must be named.
3. **bridge-at-head** — `mcp_bridge.go`: generic capabilities→MCP bridge, `--tools all`, curated-overlay shadowing — still intact at HEAD? file:line. → evidences the stretch clause.
4. **resources-at-head** — `mcp_resources.go`: Papers as `barkpark://papers/{id}` resources still listed/readable after #2588 layered HTTP on. → evidences w2-resources at HEAD, not just at merge.
5. **stdout-purity-smoke** — Run the stdio smoke + `go test ./internal/cli/ -run 'Mcp|MCP'` at HEAD; capture output. → the "run evidence" half of every stamp; distrust vacuous green.
6. **docs-trail** — CURSOR.md, HANDBOOK MCP section, `.cursor/rules/barkpark-tasks.mdc`, `docs/ops/mcp-serve-validation.md`: do documented recipes match HEAD behavior post-#2588/#2580? → wrong recipe = residue task; stale-but-true = note only.
7. **pr-trail** — Merge shas + delivered scope for #1790, #1791, #1993; plus #2588 and #2580 shas as cross-epic corroborators. → the id+sha citations the dedup law requires.
8. **cursor-path-b-remainder** — Any Cursor-specific path-B scope unbuilt? Path A = `.cursor/rules/barkpark-tasks.mdc` (d49b7c40); search ledger + repo for open Cursor items. → the honest-remainder clause of the wish.
9. **oauth-rehome** — Confirm OAuth-for-Claude.ai-remote is owned by viable-everywhere w3 (find that epic's task/paper ids). → lets the close-out disclaim it with a pointer, not a shrug.
10. **ledger-residue** — Sweep bp for open/ready/claimed tasks or drafts.* touching mcp-serve beyond the 8 children. → hard law: publish-collapse drafts; no orphaned residue at close.
11. **http-vs-stdio-seam** — How #2588 layered `--http` (`mcp_http_test.go`) on the stdio server: shared tool registry? One seam or a fork? file:line. → the corroboration story must be architecturally true, not vibes.
12. **validation-doc-freshness** — Is the `mcp-serve-validation.md` transcript (vs live guerrilla) still valid evidence at HEAD? Does guerrilla currently serve the MCP endpoint? → decides whether a fresh live transcript is needed before stamping w2-validation.
13. **epic-close-mechanics** — How did prior reconcile-and-close waves (pd-everything-editable, self-update wave 7) stamp and close their epics — exact field shapes, close verb sequence, epoch/claim handling? → our close must match house style and the task write contract.
## Survey digest (Digest phase, 2026-07-11)

12 surveyor reports in. The picture is unusually settled — this stays a **zero-build reconcile-and-close**, and both suspected wrinkles resolved cleanly (one dissolved, one confirmed as a single doc-residue slice).
### Established (evidence-anchored)

- **The epic doc carries NO acceptance_criteria of its own** — prose description only (`bp task get bp-mcp-serve-epic`: content keys are description/github/kind/lifecycle_status/priority/wave_paper/wave_status). All acceptance evidence lives on the 8 children: 47/47 criteria met, all `lifecycle_status=done`, all published, all with closed claims. Close shape therefore follows the self-update-epic precedent: rewrite the epic description as a PR-cited close story (patch+publish first), then `bp task close bp-mcp-serve-epic <worker> 0 done <reason>` — the epic is unclaimed (claim=null), so epoch 0 is accepted; there is no open-children guard; lifecycle flips go through `bp task close` ONLY, never raw mutate.
- **Every anchor clause maps to HEAD evidence** (HEAD = cbef2af2):
  - stdio `mcp serve` subcommand — `internal/cli/mcp_serve.go` (runMCPServe :60, buildMCPServer :137), PR #1790 = sha `cac9b43d`.
  - Core five tools, named EXACTLY as the anchor writes them — `mcp_tasks.go` Name: task_ready :113, task_next :152, task_show :194, task_close :226, task_create :319.
  - Manifest-machinery reuse — execManifestCommand seam; bridge handlers dispatch through the same run.go path (mcp_bridge.go:100-101).
  - Stretch capabilities→MCP bridge — registerBridgeTools mcp_bridge.go:80, shadow set :65-73, `--tools all` gate mcp_serve.go:157-161. Bridge tests 6/6 PASS at HEAD (run fresh this wave).
  - Cursor docs — CURSOR.md:76-93 documents both `~/.cursor/mcp.json` and per-project `.cursor/mcp.json`; PR #1791 = sha `398612d2` (docs-only, confirmed via diffstat).
  - Wave-2 (catalog/resources/validation) — PR #1993 = sha `94efd1f5`; Papers as `barkpark://papers/{id}` resources intact at HEAD (mcp_resources.go:91-97, :239-262).
  - Path A pointer — commit `d49b7c40` real, `.cursor/rules/barkpark-tasks.mdc` intact (last touched by #2129, content unchanged in substance).
- **Fresh run proofs already produced this wave** (not remembered green): `CC=/usr/bin/clang go build ./...` clean; 24/24 tests across all mcp_*.go files PASS at HEAD (two independent surveyor runs); TestMCPServeStdioSmoke exec's the REAL bp binary over real pipes (12.35s, byte-pure stdout, asserts the 8-tool catalog); live curl against `https://guerrilla.barkpark.cloud/mcp` → real initialize handshake (protocolVersion 2025-06-18, serverInfo barkpark-tasks) + tools/list returning all 8 tools, HTTP 200.
- **Wrinkle 1 (task_show naming) DISSOLVED** — the registered MCP tool IS named `task_show`, matching the anchor verbatim. ## The Wish (verbatim)

CLOUD CONSOLE — RECONCILE THE ANCHOR + TAKE THE HONEST NEXT LEVER. (1) verify each anchor criterion at HEAD with file:line + PR + fresh run/live proof — stamp what is TRUE (the meters/quotas criterion is likely fully evidenced by w2+w5; webhooks GUI shipped in C-waves — verify it end-to-end, not from memory). (2) For criteria with REAL gaps (candidates: Plan tab parked on plan truth cloud-17; any dead/decorative panel; audit-event coverage holes), either cut honest build slices this wave or park with a named blocker — never stamp over a gap. (3) Consume or retire the charter's stale next-wave pointers (machine-meter is DONE; live TREND eyeball is a lead/human ritual — park with recipe if unautomatable; worst-state accents stay parked on cloud-17). If all six criteria end met, close the goal via the close verb; if not, leave it open with the residue filed as children. Hard laws: never close over an unverified criterion; publish-collapse every drafts.* touch (sweep drafts.cloud-console-c10-members-usage, -c11-live-meters, -rollback-gui, -dec-*); human gates stay open with recipes; builders claim their bp task FIRST; Elixir changes wait for the Elixir Test gate; guerrilla deploys ONLY via instance-deploy.sh. File residue under cloud-console-goal.
## Strategy (wave direction)
This is the **honest-audit endgame wave**, not a feature wave. Five waves of building outran the ledger; the deliverable now is a stamp trail, not a screen. The finished state:

1. **Each of the six anchor criteria carries evidence at HEAD** — file:line + PR# + a fresh run or live-guerrilla proof — and is stamped `met:true` only where the words are actually true. Expected verdicts going in (to be overturned by evidence, not memory):
   - *meters = per-instance truth + quotas + warnings* — likely fully evidenced: w2 quota truth (#1966), w3 sampler, w4 history/sparklines, w5 machine meters (task-7100934ee7f33579, live-proven on guerrilla 2026-07-10). The honest-quota doctrine holds: ONE enforcement-backed ceiling (instances, OC11), all other meters honestly nil — if the criterion's letter demands ceilings that don't exist in plan truth, we amend the criterion with a decision note citing cloud-17, we do NOT invent ceilings.
   - *webhooks GUI-controllable* — shipped in C-waves + webhook_gone honesty (OC4); needs a true end-to-end verify (every verb reachable from the GUI, not just list).
   - *every reference tab live+tested* — the criterion's 10-tab list predates the frozen IA (D17: 4 places + Settings; capability = sub-tabs/lenses). Suspected real gap: **Plan** (parked on plan truth cloud-17). The likely honest move: reconcile the criterion against the shipped IA, stamp the live-tabs truth table, park Plan with the named blocker.
   - *every mutation audited* — the LEAST verified criterion; a route-by-route coverage map is the wave's most likely source of real build slices.
   - *no decorative UI* — sweep for dead panels; OC22's honestly-inert accent code is NOT decoration (it renders nothing) — decoration means painted-but-fake.
   - *browser never holds instance tokens* — architecture says vault-token seam is server-side only; needs a grep-proof + response-shape audit, cheap to verify.
2. **Real gaps become honest slices or parked children** — audit-event holes cut as build slices this wave if small; Plan tab parked on cloud-17 with a named blocker; live TREND eyeball parked with a human recipe if unautomatable.
3. **The ledger is left clean**: all `drafts.cloud-console-*` children publish-collapsed or retired (three dec-* records are `done` with 0/N criteria stamped — reconcile or retire them as decision records; c11 sits at 2/3 — find the unmet criterion and resolve it honestly); charter's stale next-wave pointers consumed (machine-meter DONE) or retired.
4. **The goal closes via the close verb only if 6/6 end true** — otherwise it stays open with residue filed as children. Lean: expect 1–2 small build slices max (audit holes, a webhook GUI verb gap); everything else is verification + ledger hygiene.
Quality bar: Kinsta/Vercel completeness = no dead panel, every number sourced, every lever wired. A stamp without a run proof is a lie (distrust vacuous green).
## Survey plan (12 scouts, one question each)

1. **tab-backend-truth-table** — Map the ACTUAL shipped console IA in `cloud/priv/static/app.js` (INSTANCE_TABS, SETTINGS_VIEWS, nav places) against criterion 0's list (Overview/Members/Studios/API/Datasets/Access/Activity/Usage/Plan/Settings): per tab, the serving backend route in `cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/*/router.ex` + its test file. Name any tab missing/dead/backend-less. *Why: criterion 0 needs a per-tab truth table; Plan is the suspected gap.*
2. **webhooks-gui-e2e** — Map the complete webhook GUI capability chain: which webhook verbs (list/create/rotate/deliveries/replay/delete/edit) exist in app.js, their routes, tests, and the webhook_gone/capability_unavailable honesty branch. Name any verb still curl-only. *Why: criterion 1, the epic's explicit top user priority — verify end-to-end, not from memory.*
3. **meters-quota-evidence** — Assemble criterion 2's evidence pack at HEAD: the /usage envelope's full meter set (9 + w5 machine meters), quota/warn on the instances meter (OC11 rules), warn/over rendering in SPA + CLI, sampler + history + machine meters, with file:line + PR#s + test names. State exactly which meters lack quotas and the cloud-17 dependency. *Why: this stamp should be the easiest — make it airtight.*
4. **audit-event-coverage** — Enumerate EVERY mutating route (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) in the cloud control plane and check which emit an audit/activity event (find the emission seam, grep each route). Produce the hole list with file:line. *Why: criterion 4 is the least-verified and the likeliest source of real build slices.*
5. **token-hygiene-proof** — Prove criterion 5: grep app.js + all router response shapes for any path where an instance admin/vault token could reach the browser (reveal_admin_token call sites, SSE payloads, error tuples, localStorage). *Why: architecture says server-side only — turn that into a cited proof or a named leak.*

Add a contract test mirroring federated_grant_deny_test for the scoped route: a grant-admitted non-member sees only grant-covered docs; an unowned token (positive control) sees everything; members byte-identical.

(b) REQUIRE-LOOPBACK 403 CONTRACT: /v1/data/local/search/:dataset (SearchController.search_local, pipeline :api_local) is safe solely because RequireLoopback (require_loopback.ex:20-34) halts non-127.0.0.0/8 / ::1 callers with a bodiless 403 — no test asserts this. A regression widening loopback?/1 would be caught by nothing. Add a plug/contract test: external remote_ip -> 403 halt; 127.0.0.1 and ::1 -> passes through.
